_note: Durations are typical values for planning only; they vary with variety, altitude and season. Confirm with a local extension officer.

crops.name: Apple
crops.description: Temperate tree fruit that needs winter chilling. First crop typically 3 years after planting grafted trees.

crops.name: Banana
crops.description: Frost-sensitive herbaceous perennial that needs warmth and steady moisture. First bunch about 9 to 12 months after planting.

crops.name: Black gram
crops.description: Short-season pulse that fixes nitrogen and tolerates moderate drought.

crops.name: Chickpea
crops.description: Cool-season pulse suited to drier conditions and residual soil moisture.

crops.name: Coconut
crops.description: Tropical palm needing high humidity and warmth. Starts bearing after about 6 years.

crops.name: Coffee
crops.description: Shade-tolerant tropical shrub. First harvest roughly 3 years after planting.

crops.name: Cotton
crops.description: Warm-season fibre crop with a long growing period and high potassium demand.

crops.name: Grapes
crops.description: Vine fruit that prefers warm, dry summers. Meaningful yields from about the third year.

crops.name: Jute
crops.description: Fibre crop of warm, humid, high-rainfall areas.

crops.name: Dry beans (kidney)
crops.description: Common bean grown for dry grain. Sensitive to frost and waterlogging.

crops.name: Lentil
crops.description: Cool-season pulse that tolerates drought and poorer soils.

crops.name: Maize
crops.description: Staple cereal. Needs good nitrogen supply and moisture around flowering.

crops.name: Mango
crops.description: Tropical tree fruit needing a warm, frost-free climate. Grafted trees bear after 3 to 5 years.

crops.name: Moth beans
crops.description: Very drought-hardy pulse for hot, dry conditions.

crops.name: Mung bean
crops.description: Fast-maturing warm-season pulse, useful as a catch crop.

crops.name: Muskmelon
crops.description: Warm-season vine fruit that prefers dry weather during ripening.

crops.name: Orange
crops.description: Citrus tree for frost-free, warm sites. Grafted trees bear after about 3 years.

crops.name: Papaya
crops.description: Fast-growing tropical fruit. First fruit about 9 to 11 months after transplanting.

crops.name: Dry peas
crops.description: Cool-season pulse grown in the mountains and foothills. Fixes nitrogen, so it suits rotation with maize and wheat.

crops.name: Pigeon peas
crops.description: Deep-rooted, drought-tolerant pulse that improves soil fertility.

crops.name: Pomegranate
crops.description: Drought-tolerant shrub fruit for hot, dry summers. Starts bearing in about 2 years.

crops.name: Potato
crops.description: Tuber crop for cool highland summers and lowland spring or autumn plantings. Needs loose, well-drained, slightly acidic soil and steady moisture; avoid frost on young shoots.

crops.name: Rice
crops.description: Cereal that needs abundant water, warmth and high humidity.

crops.name: Sorghum
crops.description: Drought-tolerant grain for the lowlands and foothills, planted October to December and used for flour and traditional beer. Tolerates heat and dry spells better than maize.

crops.name: Watermelon
crops.description: Warm-season vine fruit that needs sun, warmth and well-drained soil.

crops.name: Wheat
crops.description: Winter cereal of the mountains and foothills, mostly planted from April to June and harvested in early summer. Spring wheat is sown in August and September.

_lesotho_note: 'lesotho' marks how widely each crop is grown in Lesotho: staple (main field crops per FAO GIEWS and FEWS NET: maize, beans, sorghum, wheat, peas), common, possible (grown on a small scale or suited to some zones) or unsuitable (tropical crops that need frost-free, humid conditions).
